source.title: Scaling Laws in the Tiny Regime: How Small Models Change Their Mistakes
source.authors: Mohammed Alnemari; Rizwan Qureshi; N. Bagherzadeh

page_placements.theme: Calibration and predictive uncertainty need not follow test error

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps model size and measures CIFAR-100 test performance, directly testing the model-size/test-error relationship, though in different architectures and settings from the original work.
record.gate_note: The width sweeps report test accuracy and fitted test-error scaling by model size. They show no reported fall-rise-fall pattern: test error decreases across the sampled sizes, with MobileNetV2 eventually saturating. The paper does not vary training-set size or plot performance over training epochs. Its ECE inverted-U is a different measure and is not evidence about test error. The spectral-capacity discussion does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts a double-descent peak.
record.test_reason: This is a scaling-law study, not a double-descent study; Nakkiran et al. are cited only for the ECE pattern. Its width sweeps (ScaleCNN 22K–4.7M, MobileNetV2 214K–19.8M) on CIFAR-100 still report test error against model size, so they bear on V1. The setting is new: tiny models, clean labels, weight decay, Cutout augmentation, a fixed 200 epochs. The interpolation threshold is never located.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that error follows approximate architecture-dependent power laws, with decaying local exponents and MobileNetV2 saturation. They make no double-descent claim for test error; their only link to double descent is the ECE inverted U.
record.recipe_differences: It uses width sweeps and test performance, like model-size scaling studies, but trains ScaleCNN and MobileNetV2 from scratch on CIFAR-100 under a fixed 200-epoch protocol. It does not test interpolation-threshold behavior, training-time curves, or data-size variation.
record.method_sensitivity: The model-size relationship differs by architecture: ScaleCNN has a smoother exponent decline, while MobileNetV2 has oscillatory local exponents and saturates at its largest sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: ScaleCNN ECE follows an inverted U with model size: 0.013 at c=4, peaking at 0.110 at c=32, then 0.082 at c=64. MobileNetV2 ECE rises monotonically. The authors liken the ScaleCNN pattern to double descent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Calibration error, not test error, can be non-monotonic in model size, peaking at intermediate width.

record.code_released: not stated; code and result files are said to be released on GitHub upon publication, but no URL is given
record.problems: Evidence is limited to CIFAR-100 and two architectures, with width as the only scaling axis. Only 8 and 10 model sizes are sampled; the paper says these fits cannot distinguish a power law from other smooth functions. The interpolation threshold is not identified, and the largest MobileNetV2 models are described as saturated.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly measure test error across model size. ECE, class-accuracy distribution, and error-set overlap are different measures; epoch-extension spot checks do not provide an epoch-wise curve.

untested.parts: The location of the interpolation threshold and whether error peaks there. Training-set fit is reported only for the largest models.
No test-error curve over epochs; only a 400-epoch spot check (<0.3% change).
No non-deep model classes and no interpolation-point analysis.
No effective-complexity measure is used to predict a peak location. The spectral-capacity theory addresses scaling exponents only.
No label-noise or regularization sweep. Weight decay and augmentation are fixed and labels are clean.

missing.what: Training loss of the largest models (0.028, against 24.7% test error) shows they fit the training set, which bears on where the interpolation threshold lies. There are also training-loss scaling exponents (0.84 ScaleCNN, 0.30 MobileNetV2).
The training protocol conditions (weight decay 5e-4, Cutout augmentation, clean labels) are not captured as row conditions, though they matter for whether a peak is expected.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' labels are softened to limits_scope. The study never identifies the interpolation threshold and runs with standard regularization and clean labels, where the original sources report the model-wise peak to be weak or absent. V4 is removed from all rows because only deep networks are tested. The individual accuracy rows are only informative as a sequence.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not locate an interpolation threshold or test whether a peak occurs specifically near the size that just fits the training set.
No test-error curve over training epochs; models are evaluated at epoch 200. A 400-epoch spot check of three ScaleCNN configurations reports only that accuracy changed by less than 0.3%.
Only two deep-network architecture families on CIFAR-100 are studied; no non-deep model classes or interpolation-point analysis.
The spectral-capacity account estimates scaling exponents, not a shared effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across size, epochs, and sample size.
No test of label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
The study does not recount complexity using an effective number of parameters or assess whether that removes a second descent.

rows.subject: ScaleCNN size sweep (aggregate over 8 sizes)
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; evaluated at epoch 200
rows.operation_detail: Vary width and fit test error against parameter count
rows.uncertainty: ±0.002 standard deviation across five seeds; 95% CI [0.154, 0.158]
rows.note: The reported fit is decreasing error with size, not a fall-rise-fall curve.
rows.check: Drop V4: only deep nets are tested, with no non-deep classes or interpolation-point analysis. Absent is right: error falls throughout.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2 size sweep (aggregate over 10 sizes)
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; evaluated at epoch 200
rows.operation_detail: Vary width multiplier and fit test error against parameter count
rows.uncertainty: ±0.001 standard deviation across five seeds; 95% CI [0.105, 0.107]
rows.note: The reported fit is decreasing error with size, with weaker fit and saturation at the largest sizes.
rows.check: Drop V4. Error falls, then saturates; there is no rise.

rows.subject: ScaleCNN size sweep (aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; evaluated at epoch 200
rows.operation_detail: Compute finite-difference local test-error exponents between adjacent sizes
rows.value: Falls from 0.23 in the tiny regime (<100K parameters) to 0.10 near 5M parameters
rows.note: The exponent decays, but the reported error trend remains decreasing rather than showing a peak and second descent.
rows.check: Drop V4. Local exponents stay positive, so error keeps falling.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2, Figure 2 caption and following paragraph.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2 size sweep (m=0.10 to 0.35)
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; evaluated at epoch 200
rows.operation_detail: Compute local test-error exponents across adjacent width multipliers
rows.uncertainty: Pattern reported stable across all five seeds
rows.note: The local exponents oscillate, but the paper does not report a fall-rise-fall test-error curve.
rows.check: Drop V4. The exponent oscillates but stays positive (minimum 0.08), so there is no error rise.

rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; evaluated at epoch 200
rows.operation_detail: Compute local test-error exponents across increasing width multipliers
rows.note: Error improvement diminishes with size; no second descent after an error peak is reported.
rows.check: Drop V4. No numeric value is given; the text only says the exponent declines toward zero.

relationships.condition: ScaleCNN and MobileNetV2 width sweeps on clean CIFAR-100, weight decay 5e-4, crop/flip/Cutout augmentation, evaluated at epoch 200
relationships.reason: Test error falls monotonically, or saturates, with no peak across 22K–19.8M parameters (scaling_scalecnn_fit, scaling_mobilenet_fit, sc_mobile_20_to_30, sc_scalecnn_local). The threshold is not located and the setting is regularized with clean labels, so this limits scope rather than challenges.
relationships.display_finding: Test error decreased or saturated across 22K–19.8M parameters; the sweep did not establish where training interpolation occurred.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: ScaleCNN and MobileNetV2 width sweeps on clean CIFAR-100, weight decay 5e-4, crop/flip/Cutout augmentation, evaluated at epoch 200
source_check.reason: The sampled curves decrease or saturate, but the study does not locate the training-interpolation threshold or establish that its sweep brackets it. Absence of a peak in this interval therefore does not establish a condition qualifying V1's threshold-centered claim. Untested threshold behavior cannot justify limits_scope.

relation.reason: The study's own model-size versus test-error results bear on V1. Its ECE analogy alone would not constitute such a test.

tranche.reason: Width sweeps report test error against model size in a tiny-model setting, bearing on V1 despite the authors' focus on scaling laws.

source_check.notes: The absent row states describe the sampled size intervals, supported by Table 2; they do not establish absence around an identified interpolation threshold. Section 5.3 reports accuracy gains using percent signs; these are percentage-point differences in Table 2.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: ScaleCNN and MobileNetV2 width sweeps on CIFAR-100, evaluated at epoch 200
reader_labels.reason: The reported test-error fits decrease with size and the sampled accuracy results rise with size; neither architecture shows the claimed peak and subsequent second descent in the tested range (rows scaling_scalecnn_fit, scaling_mobilenet_fit, and the model-size table rows).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Two deep-network architecture families on CIFAR-100
reader_labels.reason: Both tested size sweeps show decreasing test error rather than a general double-descent curve over the sampled sizes; the study does not test the broader claim across non-deep model classes (rows scaling_scalecnn_fit and scaling_mobilenet_fit).
